now.intro: Short version: lots of shipping, slightly less sleeping. Here's the rundown.
now.shipped.1: QuestKeeper got a glow-up: a cozy tavern homepage, a redesigned character sheet, and a DM screen with Combat, Story, Players and Prep tabs.
now.shipped.2: Also new in QuestKeeper: campaigns, "Previously on…" recaps the whole table can edit, secret DM-to-player messages, and search by meaning, for when you know what you want but not what it's called.
now.shipped.3: Can You Spot It picked up a leaderboard, two Daily Prompts a day, a practice round and a How to play guide. I built those; the artwork is from our UX/UI designer, and it's gorgeous.
now.shipped.4: Reckoning Tattoo: I tuned up their website and Google Business Profile so people searching nearby can find them, see where they are, and know who's doing the tattooing and what they specialize in.
now.next.1: Launching Can You Spot It in mid-November. Season 1 of the leaderboard starts at launch, so start stretching those detective muscles.
now.next.2: Publishing the Reckoning Tattoo updates as soon as the owner signs off on the last portfolio photos.
now.next.3: Still looking for my next frontend or frontend-heavy full-stack role. Know a team that needs someone who notices friction and fixes it? I'd love to hear about it.

howIWork.intro: Five habits I brought with me from operations. Turns out they work on code too.
howIWork.01.title: 01 · Notice
howIWork.01.text: In operations, I noticed recurring friction: data that didn't match, questions asked every week. QuestKeeper started the same way.
howIWork.02.title: 02 · Ask
howIWork.02.text: I trace problems to their cause. When QuestKeeper only offered one background, Acolyte, I was sure I'd broken something. Nope: the 2014 SRD only includes Acolyte.
howIWork.03.title: 03 · Figure it out
howIWork.03.text: I learn the tool the project needs instead of waiting to feel like an expert. Can You Spot It needed React Native, Edge Functions and an AI model, and React Native was brand new to me.
howIWork.04.title: 04 · Build
howIWork.04.text: In operations, I built dashboards and SOPs. At Nugget, I built community groups and a guided review form with designers and QA.
howIWork.05.title: 05 · Explain
howIWork.05.text: I trained people and wrote instructions they could actually follow. Behind the Build does the same for my code.
btb.h2: How QuestKeeper keeps enemy stats secret
btb.text: The DM and players share one live table, but enemy HP and AC are stored separately, with access restricted to the DM. When a player attacks, a database function checks the roll against the enemy's AC and returns the result without including the AC.
about.text.1: Before software engineering, I spent years in operations and people leadership. A surprising amount of that work was really systems thinking: finding where a process broke, figuring out why, and building something better.
about.text.2: I'm also a newer D&D player, which is where QuestKeeper came from.
